_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CAT retrospectives (retro/build_cat.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open on their release days, except Q1 2008's (during the session). The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it, in either form) and the latest declared dividend (else the vintage's). Caterpillar's fiscal year is the calendar year; the recast of the FY2006-FY2008 statements (8-K of 2009-05-14) is a vintage of its own. EPS is profit per share - diluted, replaced by the company's figure where a filing publishes one excluding only one-offs (2001). Per-share figures published before the 2-for-1 split of 2005-07-14 carry their publication dates ('eps_published', 'shares_published') so the split restates them. Guides: sales and revenues as a dollar level or range ('rev_guide_usd_b', read against the last full year) or as growth ('rev_guide_pct', on the last full year unless 'rev_growth_base_b' names another base); profit per share as a dollar level or range ('eps_guide'; the 2009 guides excluding redundancy costs, with the inclusive figure in 'eps_guide_note') or as growth ('eps_growth', on the last full year unless 'eps_growth_base' names another base); words and one-sided bounds in 'rev_words' give no field. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. No later fact enters through this file.

history_vintages.why: 'Caterpillar is the leader in construction and mining equipment, and diesel and natural gas engines and industrial gas turbines in our size range' and 'Annual sales and revenues are $41.517 billion, making Caterpillar the largest manufacturer in our industry' (FY2006 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our machines and engines. Decisions to purchase our machines and engines are dependent upon performance of these industries.' and 'The rates of infrastructure spending, housing starts, and commercial construction, play a significant role in our results.' (Item 1A): demand that depends on the industries served is not earnings that are the cycle (the RCL rule), so DURABLE; no disruption theme is live for it
history_vintages.normalization: profit per share - diluted, each year from the latest filing that reports it (five-year summaries; the FY2006 10-K's 2002-2006 reflect its retrospective adoption of SFAS 123R, earlier years stay as published); a company figure excluding only one-offs replaces it (the ACN rule): 2001 $2.60 before the 2005 split (Q4 2001 release, excluding the nonrecurring charges for the sale of the Challenger tractor line, plant closings and employment reductions; GAAP $1.16 after the split, FY2005 10-K); no other year has a published figure excluding one-offs (2000's Brazilian tax adjustment and 2008's fourth-quarter tax item have none), so they stay as reported

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each annual change from the latest 10-K published by then whose statement of results (sales and revenues, operating profit, profit per share - diluted) and enterprise-wide sales table (external sales of Machinery and Engines) report both years. Seams stay in, as published: the 1999-2002 10-Ks' Engines lines are external sales (intersegment engines excluded), the FY2005 and FY2006 10-Ks restate 2003-2005 (revenue reclassifications, SFAS 123R), the 2004 change is on the split basis and the earlier ones are not (growth rates do not depend on it), Progress Rail enters Machinery from June 2006, and 2001 operating profit and profit per share include the nonrecurring charges (the values are as published; only the EPS history uses the company's figure excluding them)

price_basis: Yahoo's CAT series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1994-09-06, 1997-07-14 and 2005-07-14; no split follows 2005, so from 2008 Yahoo's close is the price as traded ($68.53 on 2008-01-04, $44.67 on 2008-12-31). Prices before 2005-07-14 are on the post-split basis in Yahoo's series, as are the per-share facts once the 'splits' record halves those published before that date.
